A currency written as a word is read now - yen, euros, pounds, francs, won, rupees, pesos and the rest, singular or plural, since the lookup retries without a trailing s - and so are the letters in front of a dollar sign, which is how a Canadian price is written wherever both dollars are in the room: C$100, US$20, A$50, HK$300, R$50. A word can be two currencies exactly as a sign can, so 100 dollars and 20 bucks answer in Canadian and American together, while a peso falls back to the Mexican one and a krona to the Swedish, each being the one a North American reader is likelier to have met. A number beside an ordinary word is still not a price: chapter 3, level 5 and Heisei 3 name no currency and answer with nothing, which is what leaves the era converter its own query. Reported 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The JLPT form is open before anybody asks for it
summary: The profile drew the form to change a JLPT certificate the moment it loaded - an editor, always open, for something that changes twice a decade - and it held one certificate, so reporting a new pass quietly erased the last one. A member holds as many as they have sat: the ladder is meant to be climbed. Certificates are rows now, listed hardest first with the year each was earned, and the card leads with the hardest and counts the rest - "N3 + 2 more". Adding one asks for the year first, because the year decides which test applies: a 2007 sitting offers Levels 1 to 4 and a 2022 one offers N1 to N5, and level 3 in 2007 is old Level 3 rather than N3, which did not exist until the 2010 restructure. The panel stays shut until it is asked for, taking one out is a control on the certificate itself, and the status - planning to sit, none, rather not say - is only asked of a member holding none, since holding one is the answer. The three answers already given were carried into rows. Who can see you was three bordered blocks for a question asked once; it is three lines. Reported 2026-09-02 by John.

name: Prices the way Japan writes them
summary: Japan counts in ten-thousands, and every price a learner meets is written that way: rent is 8万円, a salary 400万円, a flat 3,000万円. The search read the digits and dropped the unit, so 400万円 came back as four hundred yen - wrong by four decimal places on exactly the figures somebody moving to Japan needs to understand. 千, 万, 億 and 兆 are read now, and they stack the way they are written, so 3億5000万円 is three hundred and fifty million and 5万3千円 is fifty-three thousand. Units that climb rather than fall are a typo and answer with nothing, because a confident wrong figure is worse than none. The Latin shorthand is the same idea in the reader's own writing - 20k yen, 1.5m yen, $50k - and a magnitude letter is only one where a word does not follow, or the M of 20 MXN would read as a million and leave XN behind as the currency. The size cap moved with it: it was a trillion, which answered Japan's national debt of 1,300兆円 with nothing. A magnitude still needs a currency beside it, so 20k and 5万 on their own remain numbers rather than prices. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: A thousands comma is not a full stop
summary: Searching 5,000 offered the kanji for five and for zero, so a price put 零 at the top of the results. The reader matched runs of digits, and a thousands comma broke 5,000 into 5 and 000 - each read as its own number. The money parser had always dropped that comma before reading an amount; the same rule is here now and the two agree about what a number is. A comma between other digits is somebody listing two numbers and is left alone, since joining those would invent a third. The other half is why the query looked broken even spelled correctly: 五千 is the right answer to 5000 and no catalogue holds it - the spelling of a compound number is not a subject anywhere - so searching it exactly found nothing at all. The characters it is written with are offered alongside the spelling, and they are all taught: 5000 answers with 千 and 五, and 24 with 十, 二 and 四. A number written with a single character still answers with that one character only. Reported 2026-09-02 by John.

name: An amount written in words
summary: five hundred yen and twenty thousand yen name a price as clearly as 500 yen does, and neither parses - the amount must be digits today. Depends on the number library item 44 builds, which has to read words into values anyway for the reverse direction. Romaji units belong here too: a learner types 5 man yen before they type 5万円. Noted 2026-09-02.

name: A price with a word too many
summary: 100 dollars CAD and 500 Japanese yen name one amount in three tokens, and the parser takes at most one token on each side of the number, so both answer with nothing. Low value on its own; worth doing when the parser is next open. Noted 2026-09-02.

name: The facts line up where they belong
summary: The line of facts shipped an hour earlier was drawn as a list, and two of the three surfaces that show it put it inside a paragraph - the list page header and the followed-list card. No browser allows a list inside a paragraph, so the markup the server sent and the markup the browser built disagreed, React gave up matching them and rebuilt the whole tree on hydration. It reads identically and is now spans, which are legal wherever prose is. Found by reading the browser console rather than the page, which is the only place this kind of fault says anything at all.

name: Search kanji by radical
summary: The way to look up a character you cannot read: you cannot type it and you do not know its readings, but you can see 日 on the left and 月 on the right. Every search box now carries a Radicals button - the header, the phone sheet and the results page, since they are one field - and it opens the classical grid: 253 radicals in stroke-count order, the ones paper dictionaries index by. Picking narrows on all of them rather than any, so 日 with 月 is the thirty-one characters holding both, commonest first, each one a link to its page. Radicals that appear in none of what is left are dimmed rather than left as routes to an empty list, which is the whole ergonomics of the thing. The answer is pinned above the grid so a pick made at the bottom of it is still answered where you can see it. The radicals are RADKFILE's - Michael Raine's analysis of the JIS kanji, kept by the EDRDG under the same share-alike terms as the dictionary - covering 6,355 characters, rather than WaniKani's teaching radicals, which are named for what they look like and only reach the two thousand kanji it teaches. It is a dialog rather than a dropdown because 253 buttons and their answer do not fit under a field: hung from the header on a phone it ran six hundred pixels past the bottom of a screen that clips. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: A glyph for every WaniKani radical
summary: Fifteen of WaniKani's 504 radicals arrive with no character, so every surface fell through to the slug and a review of 旅 asked the member to recognise the English word "tofu". WaniKani draws those as artwork on a gated CDN that is its copyright either way. Nine turn out to be ordinary Unicode characters WaniKani never filled in, found by subtracting a kanji's known components from WaniKani's own decomposition and checking the remainder against two independent databases; the other six are shapes Unicode does not encode at all and take private-use codepoints. All fifteen are carved out of Noto Sans JP rather than drawn - Hills is 之 without its top stroke, Cactus the bottom of 虚 - so they match the site's own Japanese face because they are that face. The font ships at two weights and is scoped by unicode-range, so it is consulted for those fifteen codepoints and never disturbs the gothic, mincho, textbook or brush switch.

name: The radical picker is a command in the box
summary: The radical lookup shipped as a pill inside the search field that opened a dialog over the page, and the two halves never agreed: the query was in one place and the answer in another, a picked radical left no trace in the box, and nothing about it could be typed, copied or linked. It is a command now. Typing :rad, :radical or :radicals opens the grid under the search bar rather than over the page, picking writes :radicals 日 + 月 into the box, and the matching kanji come back as ordinary search results underneath - with the kind tabs, the keyboard and the filing column every other search already has. The query is the whole state, so it can be typed by hand, pasted to somebody and walked with the back button. The pill is gone from the field and the search bar grows while a command is in it. The reason a dialog had been chosen in the first place turned out to be a bug of its own, and a much older one: the search page's shell was clipped with overflow-hidden, so every dropdown was cut off at the shell's height. A search for "water" found ninety-one results, showed eleven and drew three. Clipping sideways is what that was for, and it now clips sideways only. Reported 2026-09-02 by John with screenshots.

name: The radical picker: a way in, and fewer rows
summary: Three things reported on the radical command. The grid gave every stroke count a row of its own, which wasted almost all of the width on the counts that hold three radicals - fourteen strokes is 鼻 and 齊 - and made the picker twice as tall as it needed to be, which is the space the answers wanted. The radicals now flow left to right in one run with the stroke count as a marker between groups, the way paper dictionaries print it, and the grid is ten rows rather than fourteen. The command was also the only way in, and nobody guesses :rad, so there is a row under the search box now - Find by Radicals, or type :rad - and the button writes the command rather than opening a panel of its own, so pressing it and typing the words land in the same place. It sits in the layout under the input rather than inside the dropdown, because the results page keeps its dropdown shut on focus so a seeded query cannot cover the results it just produced, which would have left the row permanently invisible there. And a bug: after a radical search, focusing the box again showed nothing until a key was pressed. A command in the box is the picker's own state, so focus now brings both the picker and its answer back. Reported 2026-09-02 by John.

name: Add to lists from a subject page
summary: A member could file a kanji from a search row but not from the kanji's own page, which is where you decide a character is worth keeping. The public kanji, word and radical pages carry a strip under the card with the same marks the search column uses - trouble, favourite, and a chip for each saved list - and a visitor gets the offer to join instead. Part of add-to-lists-everywhere, which keeps the glyph viewer and the explorers. Reported 2026-09-02 by John with screenshots.

name: One search box, and room to type in it
summary: The header's search was three sizes smaller than the results page's, which made one control read as two different ones - and it had grown a command language that needs room. Both boxes are the same height and the same type now, the header's collapses narrower than before when nothing is in it, and it opens far wider when it is being used, wider again while a command is in it. On a narrow desktop the section links step aside while the box is open, since somebody who has started typing is not reaching for Learn. And on the search page the header's box is gone entirely - it was a second field asking the same question a hand's width above the first - with Search named in the row instead, where the section a member is looking at belongs. Reported 2026-09-02 by John.

name: Name a radical in English
summary: The radical command could only be written in Japanese, which left the typed half of the feature useless to exactly the reader it was built for: somebody looking up a character they cannot read is usually in the same position with its parts - they can see the shape and have no way to type it. :radicals sun + moon now answers with the same thirty-one characters as 日 + 月. Names come from two sources, best first, because neither covers the set alone: the kanji dictionary for the 247 of 253 radicals that are also kanji, which is the accurate answer and costs nothing since the file is already shipped; and WaniKani's own radical names for the 199 whose character is in this set, because a member taught "fins" for ハ will type what they were taught. WaniKani's are teaching mnemonics rather than classical names - it calls 久 a raptor cage - so they answer second and never over the dictionary. A name that reaches neither answers with nothing rather than a neighbour: WaniKani draws some of its radicals instead of writing them, so "beggar" names a picture and no character here. The command's own reading changed with it. A space is inside "long time" and between 日 and 月, so it is no longer a separator: parts split on a plus or a comma, and then a part of Japanese script becomes one radical per character while a part of Latin letters stays one name however many words it holds. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: One row of options, and the row to itself
summary: Four things about the search row, reported together. Find by radicals and Add to lists were two rows of options stacked above the results; they are one row now, and the radical picker takes that row over while it is running rather than opening a second one - everything that changes how the search behaves is in the same place. The dropdown is as wide as the field it hangs from, since a fixed width left it narrower than the open box, which looked like a second control and wrapped the options onto two lines. Opening the header's box made the section links wrap to a second line while squeezing the field; the links now step aside entirely and the box takes the whole row, because somebody who has started typing is not reaching for Learn and the links are one Escape away. Escape empties the box before it closes it - one key, two things to undo, and closing first left the box still full so the next focus reopened the search somebody was trying to leave. And the radical grid can be resized: smaller, larger and reset, remembered per browser, starting larger than it shipped at. A grid of 253 characters is read by shape - 冫 and 氵 differ by one stroke - so how big it is drawn decides whether it can be read at all, and that answer is different on a phone, at a desk and for older eyes. Reported 2026-09-02 by John.

name: Size, centring and the buttons in the stroke box
summary: The stroke animation is drawn at one fixed size, and at that size the stroke numbers are too small to read - the whole point of turning them on. It takes a small S/M/L control, remembered per device. Three things beside it are out of true: the drawing is not centred in its row because the printed faces on one side and the buttons on the other are different widths, the Replay and Numbers labels sit left in buttons stretched to a common width, and the dictionary fact pills do not centre their text. Reported 2026-09-02 by John with screenshots.

name: The radicals a kanji is built from
summary: A kanji page said how the character is drawn and what it means but not what it is made of, while the RADKFILE index behind the radical search already knew the parts of 6,355 characters. Written with sits under the stroke box: each part as it is written, its English name where the dictionary has one, and a link into the radical search for everything else built from it - which is the question a reader has next. Its own block with its own credit, because the data is EDRDG's rather than WaniKani's and every block on this page names its source. The index is stored radical-first, since that is the direction a search runs, so the page's question is answered by testing 253 memberships rather than by keeping a second copy the other way round. Reachable on its own at /kanji/<character>/parts, and absent for a character RADKFILE does not cover. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The controls wait for the pointer
summary: Every card in a list carried "Add a note" printed under it in plain text and an × sitting on it, so a grid of characters read as a grid of controls and the thing the page exists to show came third. Both wait for the pointer now: they appear on the card under the cursor and on whatever has keyboard focus, and a note that has been written stays visible always, because that is content rather than a control. The × was drawn with the letter x, which read as part of the card; it is a proper mark in a circle that turns red where it will act. Reported 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The numbers hold their size, and Escape closes
summary: Two reported together. Escape emptied the search box and then did nothing: the panel left open after the clear is the recent items rather than the suggestions, and only the suggestions were in the condition, so the second press had nothing to act on. Both count now - clear, then close. And the stroke-order sizes were growing the wrong thing. The numbers are drawn inside the character's own coordinates, so asking for a bigger drawing made every number bigger by the same amount and they collided exactly as before, which is the opposite of what enlarging it was for. They are sized against the drawn width instead, so they come out the same height on screen at every setting and the extra room goes where it was wanted - between them. The largest size grew from 320 to 370 pixels and drops the four printed faces beside the drawing: somebody who has asked for the character as big as it goes is looking at the strokes, and four printed copies of it are what that width was being spent on. Reported 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The second row survives a click into a page
summary: A group's second row is how a member knows where they are, and it disappeared one click in. Absolute nav entries matched the address by exact equality, so /maps and /strokes found the Learn group and /maps/japan/gifu found nothing at all - opening a prefecture, or any stroke count, took the whole row off the page. Member-scoped pages never had it, because they match on their first path segment, which is why /grades/1 keeps its row. An absolute entry matches by prefix now, on a path boundary rather than on letters, so /mapsomething is still not a page in Maps.

name: The JLPT explorer opens when you click it
summary: Clicking JLPT Explorer looks like nothing happened: it takes about six seconds to arrive where Grades and Strokes take a tenth of a second, measured from the same page on the same server. JlptExplorerContent is a client component that imports src/data/jlptReadings.json, so 397KB of readings is shipped to the browser and parsed before the page can appear. The readings belong on the server, or behind the same catalogue lookup every other surface uses.

name: The grades page stops flashing on arrival
summary: GradeKanjiBoard seeds two pieces of state from localStorage inside the useState initializer, so the server renders the default and the browser flips it after hydration. The reveal mode is the visible one: every reading paints and then hides. Strokes shares the view-mode half of the pattern and does not flash, which points at the reveal mode as the cause. No page under Learn should flash.

name: One grid, three pages, one look
summary: Strokes, Grades and the WaniKani library each draw their own card grid, and side by side they read as three different products: different card shape, different chrome, different placement of level and status. There is already a shared pair for lists of subjects (SubjectCards and SubjectRows) and a UnifiedExplorerCard, but these three do not all go through them. Put the general look in one component and let each page pass what is genuinely its own - a stroke count, a JLPT pill, an SRS stage - rather than restating the whole card.

name: Lists gets a second row of its own
summary: Lists is a top-level section with a single child, so the header suppresses its second row and everything the page holds is stacked into the body instead. It has the same shape as Learn - several distinct collections a member moves between - so it should name them in the second row. The names should follow from what the collections actually are rather than being invented; work them out from the list kinds the code already distinguishes.

name: Print a worksheet from a list, and from the list's page
summary: A list could be turned into a writing sheet only from its card on the shelf, and only as a picked sheet carrying every one of its characters in the query string - which broke on a long list, went stale the moment the list changed, and could not be sent to anybody as a link to “my Week 1 sheet”. The page you actually read a list on offered nothing at all. A saved list is a practice source of its own now, addressed by name at /practice/list/week-1, and the sheet is titled with the list's name so a printout says which list it is. Both surfaces - the card and the list's own page - offer Worksheet and Print, the second opening the print dialog on arrival; Burned offers neither, since tracing what you already know is not practice. The list page's search box takes a line of its own on a phone, where five controls beside it had squeezed it down to four characters. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: Two sections stand aside
summary: The header carried seven sections and wrapped to two lines on a laptop, which is what made every narrow page look broken. Two of them did not earn the room: the leaderboard is the site's own front page and undeveloped besides, and Progress is history and statistics - things a member looks up occasionally rather than navigates by. Both moved into the account menu, where History and Statistics now sit beside Profile and WaniKani, which is where the rest of "about my account" already lived. The row is Study, Game, Learn, Lists and Read, and it fits on one line. The menu learned a distinction while that was open: a page rooted at the site rather than at the member is listed with Updates rather than among your own pages, because the leaderboard is everybody's and listing it under Profile would be a link to somebody else's. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The board says what is happening, and takes a wish
summary: The release board now says what is happening rather than only what is planned. In progress is its own tab, derived from the claim the board already records - not a fifth status, because two fields saying the same thing can disagree. Shelved is split into Backlog and Cancelled, which is what it always held. And the board takes a wish: an admin types a request straight into the page, it lands in the FeatureWish table, and `pnpm backlog wishes` shows an agent what is waiting with the command that files it as planned work. The timeline is a committed file the site cannot write to, so the wish list is the database half that makes a request from the website reach the board at all.

name: The JLPT counts ask WaniKani for characters it already holds
summary: The JLPT counts on the leaderboard need one static fact about each learned kanji - the character - and they were asking WaniKani for it in 200-id chunks. A member with fifteen hundred learned kanji cost eight sequential round trips on every stats computation, for data the local catalogue holds: production carries 2,102 kanji, which is every one WaniKani teaches. The catalogue answers now, in one query, and the API is kept only for ids it has never seen, so a subject added since the last sync is still counted rather than dropped. Assignments stay live, being the member's own state. The same shape the study queue and the kanji index already follow. Found 2026-09-02 while sweeping for per-render subject fetches.

name: The JLPT explorer paints before it waits
summary: The JLPT explorer's page was 13.1MB, and 9.8MB of it was word examples: every one of the 2,211 kanji carried its own compounds so that whichever one the member clicked could show them. They are read one kanji at a time, so they are fetched one kanji at a time, from a new /api/jlpt/[kanji]/words - and the panel says it is looking rather than showing an empty list while it waits. The other half was the member's own SRS state, fetched from WaniKani on every render for about 650ms before a single kanji was drawn. Account.assignmentCache already holds the whole assignments collection, refreshed by the ordinary five-minute sync, and the games and study tags already read it; getUserKanjiIndexFromCache reads the same rows without the call. Measured: 13.1MB to 1.9MB, and 1,185ms to 445ms, with the JLPT query itself falling from 381ms to 27ms. Live WaniKani assignments stay where they are needed, in the queue paths that are about to review the items.

name: The look you chose follows you off the profile page
summary: data-theme and data-jp-font were hardcoded to light and sans on the root element and changed only in the browser, by a control mounted on the profile page alone. So a member who chose Dark got dark on their profile and light on every other page: the choice did not survive a navigation. The stored value was never read back either - the comment in the control referred to a theme script that sets the attributes before paint, and no such script existed. Both preferences now live in the cookie the layout reads, so the server draws the chosen look in the first paint of every page, the same treatment the grade explorer got in 0.300.0. localStorage is gone from the control rather than kept beside the cookie: two stores that can disagree is how study mode ended up unable to turn itself off.

name: Play a game from a list you follow
summary: Practice, Match and the rest take a saved list as their pool, and only the player's own. A list a friend shares is something to read and now something to print, but not something to play. Needs a column on GameRun to remember which list a run drilled, so it is its own release rather than a rider on the worksheets. Split out of list-practice-from-shared 2026-09-02.

name: One stroke at a time
summary: The stroke order panel plays the whole character and nothing else: there is no way to hold a single stroke still and look at it, which is what somebody copying the character actually needs. A row of numbers opens under the header - closed by default, so the panel stays as quiet as it is now - and picking a number draws that stroke alone: the strokes before it in grey, the strokes after it blank, the chosen one in colour and animated so the pen direction is visible. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: A page for each part of a character
summary: The kanji page shows everything about a character at one address, so there is no way to hand somebody the stroke order and nothing else. Each panel gets a path of its own under the character - /kanji/<character>/stroke shows the stroke order alone, and the other panels follow the same shape - built from one registry so a section is defined once and rendered identically whether it is on the whole page or on its own. An unknown segment is a 404 rather than a silent fall back to the whole page. The same shape then covers radicals and words, and the share control on each panel points at that panel's own address. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The Print link is built in one place
summary: The list page appended the print flag to a worksheet address by hand, which broke the moment a shared list's address started carrying its key: the two queries ran together and Print 404ed on exactly the lists worth sharing. The card had the inverse hack - stripping a trailing flag to derive the worksheet link - so when the prop stopped carrying one, both its pills became the same link and Print silently stopped printing. listPrintHref and printNowHref are the only things that spell it now, with a test that fails if anything else does. Found 2026-09-02.

name: The same doors on radicals and words
summary: The kanji page gained an address for each of its parts; the radical and word pages, which are built from the same blocks, kept answering only as a whole. Both now take the same section segment - /radicals/leaf/related, /vocabulary/水泡/examples - from one shared registry and one shared address module, so the three public subject pages cannot drift into three different answers to the same question. A section a subject has nothing under is a 404, and every section page names the subject's own page as canonical. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The viewer asks about subject -1
summary: Surfaces that show items WaniKani never taught number their rows -1, -2, -3 down the page, so React has a key and a selection has something to hold. The review stats card passed that straight to /api/study/<id>/subjects/<subjectId>/history, which answered 400 twice on every open of a home-made list item - reproduced on a list of three such items before the fix and gone after it. The card now draws nothing for a row with no subject behind it, because there is no review history to show. The rule the filer already kept is one shared predicate, isCatalogSubjectId, rather than a > 0 test written wherever somebody remembered: the same mistake stopped filing from saving at all, because a single stand-in made the list route reject the whole PATCH.

name: Add to lists from the explorers
summary: The filing marks now reach search, the subject pages and the glyph viewer, but not the explorer grids themselves - JLPT, grades, level and study each draw their own cards and rows. SubjectCards has renderUnder and SubjectRows has renderAfterRow, so this is passing slots rather than changing the shared pair. Split out of add-to-lists-everywhere 2026-09-02.

name: Study mode cannot be turned off
summary: Study mode could not be turned off by any means. The hook returned true from its initialiser and ignored what the page had resolved from the address; it answered studyMode=off and studyMode=0 with setStudyMode(true), so the off switch turned it on; it read a stored value of any kind, including the '0' it wrote itself, as on; and it rewrote the address to studyMode=on whatever the member chose. The menu had no way out either - all four entries pick a review behaviour and every one of them turns study mode on - while the button beside it had always drawn an off state nobody could reach. So every surface gated on it stayed hidden: the JLPT explorer showed an ellipsis where meanings and readings go, and never showed a kanji's compounds at all. The decision is now one pure function, resolveStudyMode, with the address beating the browser's memory beating what it already was, and the menu offers Off above the four behaviours.

name: Kanji review stats ask under the wrong id
summary: The JLPT explorer asked for a kanji's review history under whatever the address bar held: the first segment after /users/ is the member's nickname or slug, never their account id, so every request went to /api/study/<nickname>/... and answered 404. Show review stats could never fill in, and opening any kanji logged a failed request. The account id was already a prop the component used for its other fetches, one line away from the guess. The two per-kanji lookups - this history and the compounds - now live together in useSelectedKanjiDetails, each result stored beside the kanji it belongs to, so arrowing down the list cannot show the previous kanji's history under the new kanji's glyph.

name: Step through strokes with previous and next
summary: The stroke picker offered the numbers and nothing else, so following a character stroke by stroke meant aiming at a different target for every step - and a twenty-nine stroke character wraps its numbers into a block to search through. Previous and next sit together in front of the numbers, so one repeated press walks the whole character from a control that does not move; they were tried at either end of the numbers first, which put them half a panel apart as soon as the row wrapped. The ends join up rather than going dead, because somebody who has just reached the last stroke wants to watch it built again and a stopped button sends them back to hunt for 1. The opener and the numbers also share one row now instead of stacking. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: Print is never themed
summary: Dark mode followed the page onto paper: --foreground is near-white there, so a member reading in dark mode printed almost nothing onto white paper, having first spent the ink laying a navy wash across it. Two failures, and the second hid the first - the tokens are one override, the wash is four gradients on body that the dark theme replaces on its own selector, which a bare html,body cannot outrank. The print rules move to src/app/print.css and force a monochrome palette with !important, since an @import at the top of globals.css loses every tie on source order. Filled brand pills print as outlines rather than solid black rectangles. Found 2026-09-02 by John.

name: See the whole character behind one stroke
summary: Studying one stroke drew that stroke and the ones before it and nothing else, so a first stroke was a single mark in an empty box with no sense of where in the character it belonged. The animation already draws the finished character faintly underneath and deliberately drops it the moment a stroke is picked, because an outline of everything is also what makes not-drawn-yet look drawn - so this is a mode rather than a change of default. Outline sits beside Replay and Numbers, appears only while a stroke is picked since the full drawing already has its outline, is off unless asked for, and is remembered per device. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: Print is white paper and black ink
summary: The palette override covered the site's own tokens, which is most of a page and not all of it: a panel painted with a literal Tailwind colour never asks the tokens anything, so the amber suggestion box printed a tinted block and coloured text regardless. The default inverts - every surface white, every word black - so a colour has to be opted into rather than chased down after somebody notices it on paper. The tracing sheet keeps its greys, since its faint characters are the thing being traced. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The panel keeps drawing, and keeps the outline
summary: Two switches on the stroke panel, both on and both remembered. Outline shipped a release earlier showing only while a single stroke was picked, on the reasoning that the full animation already draws its faint character - which read as the button disappearing when you left that view, and took the choice away where somebody might want the drawing clean. One switch now governs the faint character in both views. Replay was a one-shot button, so watching a stroke order twice meant finding it and pressing it again; it is a switch too, and the character draws itself over and over with a second's rest between runs - measured at 1,018ms in the browser. Without that rest the last stroke lands and the page blanks in the same instant, which reads as a glitch rather than a repeat. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: Print is the light theme, and nothing else
summary: The previous fix read 'never print in colour' as an instruction to build a printing palette: every brand colour flattened to black, every word forced black, a blanket rule over every element. It turned filled pills into solid black lozenges and spent more ink than the page it was sparing. What was actually wrong is only that the dark theme followed the page onto paper, so print now restores the ten tokens the dark theme overrides to exactly the values :root gives them, and stops. Corrected 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The catalogue says what it is missing
summary: The catalogue gap reopens every time WaniKani adds subjects and nothing says so. The admin catalogue panel already reports drift - missing levels, duplicate rows - and the count belongs beside them, but findCatalogGap reads every account's assignment cache and all 9,400 rows' relation arrays, so it cannot ride the status endpoint the panel polls. A button that measures on demand and reports the ids, next to the sync controls. Raised 2026-09-02.

name: Every block on a subject page wears the same header
summary: Stroke order draws its title in a header bar across the top of its card - a rule under it, a muted ground, the stroke count on the right - and every other block put a small label inside its padded body instead, or had no title at all. Meanings, Mnemonics and Related carried no heading, so a reader scrolling a kanji page met cards that looked like different components. One header bar in SubjectBlock, the one stroke order already used, and a title on every block that is a section of the page - taken from the same sectionTitles the section pages are named by, so a card and its own address agree. The right-hand slot is that panel's too: where its stroke count sits, a block's own control sits. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: The radicals, as a page
summary: The radical picker asks 'which kanji has these parts' from inside a search dropdown, which is the right shape for somebody mid-search and the wrong one for somebody who wants to see the radicals. This is the stroke browser's layout over the same index: counts along the top, the 253 radicals grouped by stroke below them, and the kanji containing whatever is picked. Picking is a link, so the state is in the address. The parts on a kanji page lead here instead of priming a search box. Requested 2026-09-02 by John.

name: Every radical, all the time
summary: The radicals page copied the stroke browser too literally: stroke counts along the top as a filter, so choosing '3 strokes' hid the other 208 radicals. That is the right control for 900 kanji at one count and the wrong one for 253 radicals, which are a set you scan - the filter hid the thing somebody opened the page to look through. No filter and no first step now; the count leads each row, the way the picker in search has always shown them. Corrected 2026-09-03 by John.

name: See one stroke on its own
summary: Holding a stroke still drew it in colour with every earlier stroke behind it in grey, which answers where in the character it falls but not what the stroke itself is - on a twenty-two stroke character the one you asked about is a coloured mark inside a nearly finished glyph. Only hides what is already down and leaves the single stroke on the page; with Outline on it sits over the faint whole character, which is the shape of the question: this stroke, there. A finished stroke becomes 'not yet reached' rather than a fourth state, because that is already what the animation knows how to leave wound back, and the numbers follow the same rule so nothing is numbered that is not drawn. Off by default - where a stroke falls is the usual thing to want - and remembered. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: The page says what the character is, not the stroke card
summary: Stroke order's header carried the readings and the meaning under its title - the only block on the page whose header did two jobs, now that every other card wears the same plain bar. It did that because the kanji page had no header of its own: the card was the first thing on the page, so it became one. The page names its character now, and stroke order's bar says Stroke order and the stroke count like every other card. A section drawn on its own - /kanji/X/stroke, or the panel in a modal - keeps the line, because there is no page header above it there. summaryLine moved out of the client module into lib on the way: a function exported from a 'use client' file cannot be called during a server render, which is how the page broke the first time it was wired up. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: Print one kanji as a practice sheet
summary: A sheet for one character, at /kanji/<character>/sheet and linked from the stroke panel. The character and its readings at the top, then every stroke as its own square the way a stroke-order chart shows it - all of them, so a twenty-two stroke character gets twenty-two squares rather than the first row - and then the rest of the page ruled into fifty-six empty squares to copy it into. The list sheets print a grid across many characters, a row each; this is the other shape, one character and room to work at it. The squares are the list sheets' own: Cell, TraceGlyph and StrokeStepGlyph came out of TracingSheet into sheetCells so both draw the same workbook square rather than drifting apart. Public like the character page it hangs off, because a parent printing a sheet for a child has no reason to sign in first, and a static segment so the stroke-order section keeps its address. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: The practice rows lead with a faint character
summary: The one-character sheet ruled the whole of Now You into empty squares, which asks a child to copy from a chart four inches up the page. A workbook leads the hand before it lets go: the first practice row is the character built stroke by stroke in faint, to trace over, and every row after it opens with the finished character in faint before the blanks. Nothing below the chart is highlighted - down there every mark is something to draw, and one black stroke among them would be the only one that is not. The chart at the top keeps its black stroke, since that is what says which one is new. StrokeStepGlyph grew a ghost tone for it rather than a second component. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: Worksheet goes there, Print prints, everywhere
summary: Two words for two actions, and the site had them crossed. On the list cards and the list page, Print was a link that navigated to the worksheet and asked it to open the print dialog on arrival - a button called Print that changed the page - while the stroke panel's new Print went to the one-character sheet and then did nothing, sitting in a row of its own under the drawing. One rule: Worksheet is the button that goes to a sheet, and Print exists only on a sheet, where it opens the dialog - with the scope menu where there is more than one page, as the practice sheet already does. The cards and the list page lose their navigating Print; the stroke panel's button becomes Worksheet in the header slot beside the stroke count; the one-character sheet gets the same Print button the practice sheet has. The arrive-and-print flag stays, because the sheet's own Everything choice reloads into the print layout and needs it. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: The radicals in one run
summary: A block per stroke count wasted most of its width on the counts holding three radicals and made the grid four screens tall, so the kanji a pick produced were never on screen with the radicals that produced them. It flows left to right with the count as an inline marker, in a bounded area that scrolls within itself - how the paper dictionaries print it and how the picker in search has always drawn it. Corrected 2026-09-03 by John.

name: The kanji page introduces itself like the others
summary: A radical and a word open with an identity card - the glyph, the English name, its type and level as pills, then meanings and readings under a credit. A kanji opens with a bare line of text above the stroke order box, so the one page most people arrive on is the one that looks unfinished beside its two siblings. Parity is structural: the same card in the same slot, fed by what the kanji page already knows. Reported 2026-09-03 by John.

name: One sheet for a list and for a single character
summary: The one-character practice sheet was a second implementation beside the practice sheet the lists print - its own page, its own component, its own row grammar (faint model leading each row, no heading line) and none of the options, so the two looked like two products. There is one sheet now: TracingSheet takes the characters it is given and a Fill the page option shares the page's rows between them - one kanji takes the whole page, two take half each - on top of whatever rows each needs of its own, the stroke chart in Stroke order mode or the trace row in Trace mode. The character page's Worksheet links into the member's practice sheet with that character picked, Stroke order on and the page filled, so it has the same header, the same Practise, Sheet and Options rows, the same square sizes and the same Print. /kanji/X/sheet, KanjiPracticeSheet and its copy are deleted. The faint-first-row grammar of 0.333.0 goes with them: the shared row is the workbook's - the finished character to copy, faint repeats to trace, blanks to write - and a variant belongs as an option on this sheet, not a fork. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: The header holds one line, whatever the width
summary: Between about 1000 and 1280 pixels the top row broke after LISTS and put PROGRESS and READ on a second line, and the section row stacked its pages into a column - so the header changed height as the window moved and the page below it jumped. Both rows now hold one line and scroll instead, the way the phone row already did, and the release codename waits for 1280 rather than taking the room STROKES needed. Reported 2026-09-03 by John, who had asked for this before.

name: Zoom in on the map, and get about
summary: Kanto is eight prefectures inside a thumbnail: on a whole-country map Saitama and Gunma are a few pixels of the same grey. Three zoom steps rather than a free zoom, with drag, arrow keys and +/-/0 to move around, and the window clamped so a drag that runs off the edge stops rather than framing open sea. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: A worksheet says it came from UmaKuma
summary: The practice sheet carries no brand at all: on screen the page has the site's navigation and nothing that says UmaKuma, and on paper - where a sheet is photocopied, handed to a child and pinned to a fridge - there is nothing at all. Every other page wears the banner. The sheet wants the brand minimally on screen, the mark and the name above the title, and more minimally still on paper: one quiet line, the name and the address, in the grey the rest of the printed sheet uses, so whoever picks the page up knows where it came from and where to get another. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: The name's kanji, drawn like every other kanji
summary: The map panel drew the characters of a place name as coloured boxes of its own making: no meaning, no reading, and no way to keep one, on a site where every other place a kanji appears carries all three. It uses the shared subject card now, which brings the reading, the meaning, the link to the character's page and the filing column with it. Double-clicking a region zooms one step in on it. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: The values open under the chip you clicked
summary: Choosing a source on the practice sheet opened its levels below Trace / Stroke order / Reference, because the source chips and the sheet chips shared one wrapping nav - the list somebody had just asked for appeared under an unrelated row, two lines from the chip they pressed. Three rows now, in the order they are read. Found 2026-09-03 by John.

name: Okinawa stays in its box, and Escape puts a region down
summary: Zooming dropped the inset, so Okinawa left its box off the south-west of the mainland and was redrawn where it really is, on top of the coast the reader was looking at. The inset held only while the whole country was in view, which stopped being true the moment the study map could zoom. Centring had the same fault from the other side. Escape now clears the chosen region at desktop width, where there is no modal to close. Found 2026-09-03 by John.

name: Map kanji as pills
summary: The characters of a place name are the same small pills the kanji page uses, with the Text on toggle, not the large explorer cards.

name: One chip for every inline kanji
summary: Every inline kanji, radical or word across the site is drawn through the shared pill; hand-rolled chips and misplaced large cards are replaced.

name: Mark what you know, and where you have been
summary: A member marks each prefecture, state or province 'I know it' or 'Needs practice', and separately flags the ones they have been to - the map paints all three in soft greens, ambers and a blue outline. Two facts rather than one. One new table, MapRegionMark, unique per member per region. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: Say the answer, not just show it
summary: A search for 500 yen answers with what it converts to and never with how to say it. The amount a learner most wants from a price is 500円 and ごひゃくえん - the currency answer had no Japanese form at all when the query was already in yen, and the reading the number answer works out sat on a line the search dropdown does not draw. An answer carries its reading as its own field now, so every surface that shows an answer can say it aloud. Reported 2026-09-03 by John.

name: The chosen region, drawn on its own
summary: On the country map Kagawa is four millimetres of grey and Rhode Island is smaller than the word for it, so the shape - the one thing a map is for - is the thing you cannot see. The panel draws the chosen region filling its width, neighbours in outline so it reads as a place rather than a blob. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: Escape puts the search away
summary: Escape on a focused search box empties it, and on an empty box it closed the dropdown and left the field open and focused - so the box a member wanted rid of stayed on screen, widened, with the cursor still in it. An empty box now goes away on Escape: the panel closes, the field gives up focus and shrinks back, and the phone sheet closes with it. Reported 2026-09-03 by John, who had asked before.

name: Releases open at the month you are in
summary: The releases page prints every month at full length, so the page opens on a wall of entries and the month somebody came for is a long scroll away. Each month becomes a section that folds: the current month open, the rest closed, any of them toggled by hand, and the choice remembered per device so a refresh does not undo it. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: Filter the releases by what they touched
summary: Every release is already tagged by area, and the tags are shown without being usable: there is no way to ask for the games work, or everything that touched search. The page lays out every area it holds with a count beside it, and choosing one filters the list. Areas only - a feature and a bug are not the same kind of tag. Requested 2026-09-03 by John.

name: Print without leaving the page
summary: Printing a list opens /users/<name>/practice/list/<slug>, which switches the header's section from Lists to Learn - you asked to print and the site took you somewhere else. A print modal would keep the reader where they are and be callable from anywhere a printable thing is shown. Requested 2026-09-02 by John, twice. Tabled in the backlog 2026-09-03 at his request.

name: A toggle for the reading and the English
summary: The map panel's kanji cards show the meaning and the reading together. John asked for the shared component 'with a toggle, the english/reading'; showing both was a judgement call made without flagging it, and the grade explorer already has the reveal control this would reuse. Raised 2026-09-03 by John.

name: The region shape is drawn tiny
summary: The side panel draws the chosen region on its own so the shape can be seen, and the shape is a few millimetres in the middle of the whole country. The window is padded by nine tenths of the region's longest side and is nearly square, while the frame is two and a half times as wide as it is tall, so the map scales to the height and shows two or three times more country than the window asked for: Hokkaido's window comes out larger than Japan. The shape should fill the frame it is given, with only enough room around it to place the region among its neighbours. Reported 2026-09-03 by John.
